text:
alice.optih: hey - we're trying to onboard OptiHealth but the client is getting 401 when hitting /v1/generate. I created a project, but can't find an API key in the console. Can someone check? :wave:

maria.support: hey alice, sorry about that. can you paste the response body you're seeing and the project id you created? also which auth method did you use (email signup vs SSO)?

alice.optih: response: 401 Unauthorized, body: {"error":"missing_api_key","message":"no api key provided"}
project id in console is optihealth-prod-12
we signed up via Okta SSO (company SSO).

maria.support: thanks. quick checklist: 1) are you using the project id in the header X-Redwood-Project? 2) check Console > API keys — do you see any keys listed at all?

alice.optih: i only see the project in Projects list but no keys tab shows up for me. clicking "API keys" gives a permissions error.

maria.support: aha. that sounds like a permissions scoping issue for SSO-provisioned orgs. i'll escalate to devex and add some repro steps. assigning kevin for logs.

maria.support: @kevin.sre can you grep auth logs for alice.optih org around 2026-03-13 15:00 UTC? their user id is u_8142

kevin.sre: on it. pulling auth audit now. short summary: user's Okta assertion was accepted, account created, but the provisioning hook didn't assign the user to the "org-admin" role in the project metadata. console hides API key creation UI unless you have project-level Admin role — that's why she can't see or create keys. looks like a mapping gap between our SSO mapping rules and new Okta group names.

li.devex: thanks @kevin.sre. i can repro locally with a test Okta assertion that maps to a non-admin role. the UI gating is by design (only org-admins can create API keys). options: 1) have account admin invite the user with Admin role; 2) support can elevate this user temporarily; 3) fix the SSO mapping rule to map Okta group OptiHealth-Admins to org-admin.

maria.support: alice, do you have a teammate who signed up as the initial billing contact or admin? if so, they can invite you as admin. if not, we can temporarily elevate your account while we fix mapping. which would you prefer?

alice.optih: we only have one person who set up SSO & they left last week :/ we'd prefer you elevate us so we can create keys. we need to give our devs a key asap.

maria.support: understood. @jordan.account can you confirm we can escalate temporary admin elevation for OptiHealth? need approval to perform account role change and document it on the ticket.

jordan.account: confirmed — ok to elevate one user to org-admin for 24 hours for onboarding. log the change in the customer's account notes.

maria.support: thanks. @kevin.sre can you perform the elevation? and while you're at it, can you generate an API key ourselves and share it in a secure transcript so they can test immediately?

kevin.sre: will do. steps i'm running now: 1) add u_8142 to project role org-admin in identity service 2) trigger cache invalidation so console shows API keys UI 3) create an API key named "onboard-optih-2026-03-13" 4) rotate/remove after they've confirmed.

kevin.sre: done step 1-2. alice, can you refresh your console and confirm you see "API keys"?

alice.optih: i see it now :tada: i can create a key. but when i call the API with the key i created i still get 403 Forbidden: {"error":"project_mismatch","message":"api key not valid for project optihealth-prod-12"}

maria.support: ok that's new. can you paste the curl you're using? and confirm which project header is being sent?

alice.optih: curl -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \n -H "Authorization: Bearer sk_live_XXXXX" \n -H "X-Redwood-Project: optihealth-prod-12" \n -d '{"prompt":"hi"}'

li.devex: project_mismatch means the key was created under a different project than the header. I see kevin created the key under the default org project (optih-staging-1) by accident — my bad, when I created via the admin API I didn't set project_id param. kevin, can you revoke that key and recreate in optihealth-prod-12?

kevin.sre: revoking now and re-creating with explicit project_id. creating key "onboard-optih-2026-03-13-v2" under optihealth-prod-12. sending the key via SupportSecureLink in the ticket (not pasted here).

deploy-bot: [audit] api_key.create by kevin.sre for project=optihealth-prod-12 id=key_9a3f

alice.optih: re-tested with the new key, success 200, tokens returned. thanks so much. can you summarize the root cause so we can close the loop with our security team?

maria.support: summary: initial SSO provisioning created a user without org-admin role due to group mapping mismatch, preventing API key UI access. support elevated the user temporarily to allow key creation. a follow-up configuration error created the first key under a different default project (missing project_id on create), causing project_mismatch errors. resolution: we created correct key in optihealth-prod-12, revoked the stale key, and patched SSO group mapping rule to map OptiHealth-Admins -> org-admin.

li.devex: action items: 1) update Okta mapping rule and deploy to staging (PR #1543) 2) add a validation in admin API to require explicit project_id on key create when caller is org-admin (so keys can't land in default project unexpectedly) 3) add a short doc in onboarding playbook about SSO role mapping checks. assigning myself and kevin.

maria.support: alice, i'll also log a 24-hour admin elevation in the account notes and mark ticket for follow-up with jordan.account to confirm closure after 48 hours. any other asks?

alice.optih: that's perfect. please also send the timeline and who changed what to our security officer (cc'ed in support ticket). thanks again!

maria.support: will do. closing loop: created key, verified API calls, updated mapping rule draft, flagged admin elevation. leaving this thread open until jordan confirms ticket closure. :lock:
